title: Environmental recurrence selects a costly memory-use policy across two operator bundles without a resolved one-bit population benefit

creators.name: Chen, Jack
creators.affiliation: Frederick Sequencing and Genomics Core; Advanced Biomedical Computational Science (ABCS); Frederick National Lab for Cancer Research; National Institutes of Health

description: Three prospective abstract computational studies in two operator bundles ask whether lag-two environmental recurrence selectively enriches a mutable policy for using a supplied one-record private cache when each retrieval replaces a fresh proposal, and whether that selection converts into population performance. In Study 001, recurrence strongly enriched the allele while the recurrent ACTIVE-minus-SHAM population-accuracy contrast was bounded below the prespecified one-correct-bit scale with sign unresolved; the ZERO-law contrast was descriptively adverse. In Study 002, directional cache information further amplified selection, but its total population-accuracy effect through evolved policy use was bounded below the positive one-bit scale with sign unresolved. In Study 003, an independently implemented large-alphabet torus operator bundle with graded circular loss and tournament survival, recurrence-attributable selective enrichment recurred, P_abs was bounded below the positive 1/32 maximal-loss scale with sign unresolved and P_rec was unresolved. The selection/performance separation thus recurred across two operator bundles at the declared scales. The cache architecture was supplied; retention and retrieval were not separated; effects in Study 003 cannot be attributed to individual operator components. The 22, 19 and 22 saved estimate records are separate families, not independent replications. A Study 003 audit-header interface failure was resolved by a 12-byte normalization of a derived audit tree; original outputs are preserved. Audits were internal. Research preprint; not externally peer reviewed. Manuscript/data CC BY 4.0; original code MIT; AI assistance disclosed.
